subject: Post-demo: Redwood vs hyperscalers — qualification & unit-econ next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Redwood vs hyperscalers — qualification & unit-econ next steps

John — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from our call)
- Goal: replace 1-2 API endpoints that power Acme's content-generation feature (peak 120 qps, P95 latency target <= 300ms) while cutting per-token spend vs current hyperscaler setup.
- Key constraints: data residency (US-only), strict audit logs, and ability to burst for seasonal spikes.

What we (Redwood) will deliver next (by end of week):
1) A concise per-1M token cost model comparing Redwood hosted + Dedicated burst option vs two hyperscalers (incl. assumed batch sizes). See attached econ sheet for the template. (attachment: redwood-infer-econ-sheet.xlsx)
2) A short benchmark plan to validate: single-request latency at target prompt lengths, batching at sizes 1/4/8/16, and a KV cache hit-rate simulation (we'll use your sample traffic).
3) A summary of security options to meet data residency + logging (SOC2 controls + VPC plan).

Asks from your side:
- Confirm the sample traffic file I attached (acme-traffic-sample.json) is representative of your steady-state/peak spike mix.
- Confirm which hyperscalers/APIs you want explicitly compared (we noted Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B).

Attachments: redwood-infer-econ-sheet.xlsx, demo-recording.mp4, acme-traffic-sample.json

Next steps / timeline:
- Wed (11/25): Redwood sends initial per-1M token TCO + benchmark plan
- Mon (11/30): Redwood publishes run results + recommended configuration (batching, cache, quantization profile)

If that timeline works, we'll kick off the bench next day and keep the tests reproducible so you can run them internally as well.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0128

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood vs hyperscalers — qualification & unit-econ next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The traffic sample looks good overall; the 95th percentile prompt lengths are a bit longer than your sample (we'll attach a revised sample). Peak qps is usually 110–130 during sales events.
- Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B are fine. Also include the managed LLM endpoint from CloudX (they're getting quoted internally).
- On the procurement side, we need an estimate of monthly committed spend vs on-demand (we have procurement thresholds that trigger a CRO review).
- Data residency: US-only is required; if you show a clear audit log path and KMS integration that helps.

One more ask: can you show the effect of cache hit rates at 20%, 50%, 80% for per-token economics? That will be a major lever for us.

I'll loop in legal later if we get to POC. Thanks — John

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-demo: Redwood vs hyperscalers — qualification & unit-econ next steps

Forwarding John's notes — see inline plan and owner assignments below.

Internal plan (owner / <48h deliverables):
- Jordan: update the econ sheet to show per-1M token cost across scenarios including cache hit rates at 20/50/80%, committed monthly vs on-demand, and error budgets for latency. Use assumptions for batch sizes 1/4/8/16.
- Connor: spin up a short, reproducible benchmark harness that simulates their traffic (will use acme-traffic-sample.json). Run Redwood hosted + Dedicated profile, Hyperscaler A, Hyperscaler B, and CloudX managed endpoint. Capture cost-per-1M tokens and P95 latencies.
- Marissa: draft a short one-pager comparing differentiators (routing/fallback, KV cache, rollout controls, private deployment options, SLA terms) for exec readout.

Note: keep the attachments small — send links when possible. I'll coordinate the HubSpot deal update once we have the initial TCO model.

— Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood vs hyperscalers — qualification & unit-econ next steps

John — quick update: we ran an initial pass over the weekend and have a draft attached in Drive. Highlights (high level):

- Baseline per-1M tokens (assumptions: 1x standard model, no cache, batch=1): Hyperscaler A $210, Hyperscaler B $195, CloudX $230, Redwood hosted $160 (Redwood Dedicated baseline with burst amortization shows $145).
- Latency (P95) at average prompt lengths: Hyperscalers ~220–340ms (varies heavily with batch), Redwood hosted ~190ms, Dedicated ~160ms.
- Cache impact: moving from 20% -> 80% hit rate shifts Redwood effective cost down ~43% (details in Drive sheet).

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/ACME-2026 | Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-econ

Next steps we propose:
- Wed (12/02): run controlled benchmark with exact prompt set and batch sweep (1/4/8/16) — Connor to lead.
- Thu (12/03): deliver final per-1M token TCO with committed vs on-demand scenarios + recommended config (batch size, cache policy, quantization profile).

Connor — can you confirm you have the harness and estimated run time? Marissa — I'll review the one-pager and add the audit-log + KMS notes for US-only residency.

Thanks — we'll keep the results reproducible so Acme can re-run.

Regards,
Jordan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
